correctness.rationale: For the literal integral 52-line quartic equation in Veniani Example 5.5, independently checked 8F=-Q under the invertible odd-characteristic coordinate change. The fifteen integer principal minors are -4,0,4,0;-4,-25,-1,-1,-1,-4;-24,8,24,-8;64, so nonzero determinant primes are only 2,3,5. Kernel-support analysis over algebraic closures gives exactly two axis singularities in odd characteristics other than 3/5, eight extra points in characteristic 3 and two extra in 5. Independently evaluated local affine Hessian determinants at all five singularity types (nonzero mod p), hence A1 nodes. In characteristic 2 F=H^2(x0*x3+x1*x2), all four partials generate H^2 times the irrelevant coordinate ideal, and projective saturation yields (H^2); G is smooth with two-line intersection with H=0. The determinant argument, not finite enumeration of primes, establishes the all-prime claim. No line-count statement beyond prior work.
